name: Bob Menendez
role: U.S. senator from New Jersey (2006–2024); chair of the Senate Foreign Relations Committee (2021–2023); U.S. representative (1993–2006)
summary: Menendez is a mainstream Democrat whose record is strongest on foreign policy: he backs NATO, Ukraine, sanctions and arms control, and voted for Wall Street reform, the Affordable Care Act and comprehensive immigration reform. He voted for gun limits and abortion-rights legislation, and for both the Defense of Marriage Act (1996) and its repeal (2022).

abortion-legal.rationale: Voted yes on cloture for the Women's Health Protection Act (S4132, May 2022) and against the 1993 Hyde funding-restriction amendments in the House.

death-penalty.rationale: In April 1994 voted against the amendments that would have removed the federal death-penalty provisions from the crime bill and for the McCollum amendment adding death-penalty procedures.

end-foreign-alliances.rationale: Voted yes to ratify NATO accession for Finland and Sweden (Aug 2022, 95-1) and voted for the 1995 NATO Revitalization and Expansion Act amendment.

keep-nuclear-weapons.rationale: Said in June 2021 that New START gives the flexibility needed to maintain a safe, secure, modern and effective nuclear deterrent.

limit-guns.rationale: Voted for the Brady Act (1993), the 1994 assault-weapons ban and the 2013 Senate assault-weapons amendment; these limit some guns, not ownership as a whole.

no-bailouts.rationale: Voted no in April 2009 on amendments to end TARP bailouts and bar bailouts for auto makers, and yes on the 2010 financial-stability bill.

open-lgbt-military-service.rationale: Voted in 1993 for the amendment codifying Don't Ask, Don't Tell, then yes on the December 2010 bill (HR2965) repealing it.

reduce-immigration.rationale: Voted yes on cloture and passage of the 2006 comprehensive immigration reform bill (S2611) and on cloture of the 2007 bill (S1348).

same-sex-marriage.rationale: Voted for the Defense of Marriage Act in 1996 (House), then for the Respect for Marriage Act repealing it (cloture and passage, Nov 2022). The votes split across 26 years.

torture-always-illegal.rationale: Voted yes on the 2015 Senate amendment to HR1735 reaffirming the prohibition on torture.
